citation.title: Self-directed online machine learning for topology optimization
citation.authors: Changyu Deng, Yizhou Wang, Can Qin, Yun Fu, Wei Lu

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: Self-directed online learning reduces objective evaluations and computational time for heuristic topology optimization; the abstract reports a two-to-five-order reduction relative to direct heuristic methods.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Abstract states 2–5 orders of magnitude less computational time; represented as a range of 100× to 100,000×, with 100 used as the numeric field's lower bound.
claim.alternatives: The abstract also claims better results than tested state-of-the-art algorithms; particular problem comparisons appear in Results.

baseline.classical_method: Generalized Simulated Annealing, Binary Bat Algorithm and Bat Algorithm
baseline.implementation: Heuristic optimizers use the learned surrogate in SOLO; direct heuristic baseline also evaluates the objective by FEM
baseline.solver: Finite element method for objective evaluation
baseline.hardware_classical: Intel i7-8086K CPU and Nvidia RTX 2080 Super GPU (Supplementary Table 1; compute split by step)
baseline.hardware_ml: Intel i7-8086K CPU and Nvidia RTX 2080 Super GPU (Supplementary Table 1)
baseline.problem_size: Two compliance problems, fluid-structure cases, heat-transfer case, and truss problems; compliance examples include 5×5 and 11×11 design variables (Abstract; Results and Supplement)
baseline.classical_time: Abstract gives direct heuristic method comparison as 2–5 orders slower; objective FEM calls take <0.5 s in compliance examples (Supplementary Table 1 discussion)
baseline.ml_time: Loop times listed in Supplementary Table 1; no single ML runtime in abstract
baseline.training_time: Reported by loop in Supplementary Table 1
baseline.data_generation_cost: Dynamically generated FEM-labelled samples; numbers of FEM evaluations compared as 10^5–10^8 reduced to 10^2–10^4 (Supplementary Table 1 discussion)
baseline.quality_metric: Compliance/objective, heat charging time, fluid pressure loss, or truss weight, depending on problem
baseline.quality_gap: Problem-specific objective values and comparisons are reported in Results; no single aggregate gap.

R1.evidence: Abstract: computational time is compared with direct heuristics, without a stated equal-quality or matched-budget comparison.

R2.evidence: Methods and Supplementary Table 1: the article reports direct heuristic comparisons and shared computing hardware; no R2 failure criterion is established.

R3.evidence: Methods and Supplementary Table 1 describe dynamically generated data and DNN training/optimization overhead, but no break-even number of uses is given.

R4.evidence: Results use FEM objective evaluations and volume constraints, but systematic infeasibility/failure rates are not reported.

reporting.n_test_cases: Two compliance problems, two fluid-structure problems, one heat-transfer problem and three truss problems (Abstract; Results).

notes: Queue title identifies an earlier title for arXiv:2002.01927. Per duplicate/version rule, coded the latest arXiv v8 full text. Public source code and data are identified, but a permissive license and runnable benchmark were not confirmed. Fluid-structure examples are outside scope, but the article also includes structural compliance optimization.
